sheet-89-1.description: Northern end of North Arlington in March 1922, drawn at 100 feet to an inch on an additional sheet of the Harrison and Kearny volume. The part runs from the Passaic River and River Road on the west to Gold Street on the east edge, and from the sheet's top margin (Locust and Albert) south to Eagle and Front. The streets west of High Street are irregular: Locust, Hawthorne Avenue, Crystal, Duncan and Eagle meet River Road and a jogging West Street, and a diagonal street lettered North runs from West Street to High Street across block 8. East of High Street the grid is regular, with Albert, Biltmore, Crystal, Duncan, Eagle and Front crossing to Gold Street; Riverview Avenue begins at Duncan. Most lots are laid out but only partly built: scattered frame dwellings, automobile garages, sheds and poultry houses, a few brick-veneered houses and stores, a Pentecostal church on Biltmore, and a hollow tile works. Joseph A. Klitch's concrete block factory stands on West Street near Locust. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along Albert, Biltmore, Duncan and Front, and the lettering gives street widths of 40 to 70 feet. The southern part of block 21, between Eagle and Belmount, is open ground carrying only a few scattered buildings; the mask of this part stops in the middle of that block, where part 2 takes over. The Passaic River is drawn along the west edge with its flow arrow. The adjoining sheet 90 is referenced on the east edge.
notes: Duncan is Stover Avenue today.
Hawthorne Av. is probably today's Bayliss Street; not used as control.
The diagonal street lettered North corresponds to the western part of today's Biltmore Street.
Modern River Road junctions along this part lie about 12 m off the drawn River Rd and were left out of the control; the west side is placed by West Street.
Gold Street at the east edge is drawn only partly and was left out of the control (sheet 90 draws it in full).
Joseph A. Klitch concrete block factory on West Street.

Map, 100 ft. North end of North Arlington between the Passaic River (River Rd) and Gold St: Locust, Albert, Biltmore, Hawthorne Av, North, Crystal, Duncan, Eagle, Front, West, High, Riverview Av; Belmount Av and Sunset Av below the open block 21. Configured as two parts: part 1 (main map, Locust to Front) and part 2 (Belmount Av to Sunset Av), split across the open block 21 because the two halves do not fit one transformation (4 to 7 m residuals combined, about 1 m apart). Duncan is Stover Avenue; North is the west end of Biltmore Street; Hawthorne Av probably Bayliss Street. Modern River Road is about 12 m off the drawn River Rd north of Eagle (left out of part 1); Gold St at the east edge is left out (drawn on sheet 90).

sheet-89-2.description: Southern strip of sheet 89 of the 1922 North Arlington additions, drawn at 100 feet to an inch: the blocks between Belmount Avenue and Sunset Avenue from River Road and the Passaic River east to Prospect Avenue, with the lower half of the open block 21 north of Belmount. Blocks 22 and 23 are divided into narrow building lots, mostly vacant; frame dwellings, automobile garages and a few stores stand along Sunset Avenue near Prospect Avenue and at the River Road end. A large frame dwelling with a brick-veneered wing stands in block 21 north of Belmount. Riverview Avenue crosses the strip between Belmount and Sunset. Water pipes run along Belmount and Sunset with hydrants at the corners, and River Road is drawn along the river bank. The scale bar and copyright line sit in the bottom margin, where sheet 91 continues to the south. This strip was georeferenced separately from the upper part of the sheet because the two did not fit one transformation: the junctions of the two halves disagreed by 4 to 7 m in a single fit and agreed to about 1 m when fitted apart.
notes: Split from part 1 across the open block 21, where there is no line on the sheet: the strip and the upper map do not fit one transformation (residuals of 4 to 7 m in a combined fit).
Belmount Avenue now runs straight through to Ridge Road; the 1922 sheet shows it from River Road to Prospect Avenue.

Configured as two parts: part 1 (main map, Locust to Front) and part 2 (Belmount Av to Sunset Av), split across the open block 21 because the two halves do not fit one transformation (4 to 7 m residuals combined, about 1 m apart). sheet-90.description: Sheet 90 of the 1922 North Arlington additions, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The upper left shows the blocks from Gold Street to Kearny Avenue between Albert and Front (blocks 1 to 6), with narrow lots, scattered frame dwellings and garages, and the Crystal Laundry on Biltmore. Below Front the sheet follows Kearny Avenue south to Sunset Avenue and Franklin Place: York Road and Willis Road with their lots (blocks 7 and 8), St. Paul's P.E. Mission church and parish house near Prospect Avenue, North Arlington Public School No. 1 and the North Arlington Municipal Building on the east side of Kearny Avenue, and Our Lady Queen of Peace Roman Catholic Church between Worthington Place and Franklin Place. Large parts of blocks 9 and 21 are open land. Water pipes run in most streets, with a 20 inch main of the East Jersey Water Company and an 8 inch pipe along Kearny Avenue. The upper right of the sheet carries the key map of North Arlington at 1,000 feet to an inch with the population (2,000), water and fire department notes; it lies outside the mask of this annotation. The street lettered Kearny Av. is Ridge Road in North Arlington today.
notes: Kearny Av. is Ridge Road today (Kearny Avenue keeps the name only south of Belleville Turnpike).
Duncan is Stover Avenue today.
Worthington Pl. is not in today's street data under that name; probably today's Church Place. Not used as control.
The key map of North Arlington (1,000 ft to an inch) in the upper right is cut out of the mask.
North Arlington Public School No. 1, Municipal Building, St. Paul's P.E. Mission, Our Lady Queen of Peace R.C. Church, Crystal Laundry.

Map, 100 ft. Gold St to Kearny Av (Ridge Road today) from Albert to Front, and Kearny Av south to Sunset/Franklin Pl with York Rd, Willis Rd, Worthington Pl, Prospect Av. Upper right carries the key map of North Arlington at 1,000 ft to an inch, cut out of the mask. One part.

sheet-91.description: Sheet 91 of the 1922 North Arlington additions, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the river side of the borough from Sunset Avenue south to Belleville Turnpike. River Road runs down the sheet beside the Passaic River. In the north, blocks 2 to 8 between River Road, Bathurst Avenue, River View Avenue and Prospect Avenue are cut into narrow building lots along Ilford, Hendel and Melrose Avenues, with scattered frame dwellings and garages. South of these the land is open: block 9 holds a few dwellings and barns, and below it lie the abandoned Pumping Station of the Jersey City Water Works, with a caretaker living on the premises and machinery left in the buildings, and the Atlantic Comb Works (celluloid works) east of River Road, described as numerous brick and frame buildings with admittance refused. A drive runs along the south side of the comb works. At the bottom, Belleville Turnpike crosses the river on an iron bridge carrying 42 inch and 30 inch water pipes, with an oil service station at the River Road corner. The rest of the lower sheet is open ground.
notes: Detected with ink_below_paper 100 on this part; at the default only 5 junctions were found.
Abandoned Jersey City Water Works pumping station; Atlantic Comb Works (celluloid).

Map, 100 ft. River Rd and the Passaic River from Sunset Av to Belleville Turnpike: Bathurst Av, River View Av, Prospect Av, Ilford, Hendel, Melrose Av; abandoned Jersey City Water Works pumping station, Atlantic Comb Works. One part. Detector ink_below_paper 100 for this part.

sheet-92.description: Sheet 92 of the 1922 North Arlington additions, at 100 feet to an inch, shows the centre of the borough along Kearny Avenue from Sunset Avenue south to Belleville Turnpike. West of Kearny Avenue, the blocks between Prospect Avenue and Kearny along Sunset, Ilford, Hendel and Melrose Avenues are lined with frame dwellings, many with garages; south of Melrose lies the open block 4 with a disused reservoir. East of Kearny Avenue the streets Franklin Place, Abbot Place, Wesley Place and Inman Place run to Morgan Place, and further south Union Place, Morgan Place and Rutherford Place cross Ridge Avenue down to Belleville Turnpike, a closely built district of dwellings with a few stores. The Fire Department Hose Co. No. 1 stands on Kearny Avenue near the turnpike, beside a group of brick stores. Nichols Beaver Farm occupies the top right corner. Water pipes run in every street, with the 42 inch Jersey City main and a 30 inch pipe along Belleville Turnpike and a 20 inch East Jersey Water Company main up Kearny Avenue. The neighbouring sheets 90, 91, 93, 79 and 80 are referenced at the edges, with Pleasant Place and Grand Place lettered below the turnpike.
notes: Kearny Av. is Ridge Road today.
Ridge Av. is Harding Avenue today.
Abbot Pl. is Abbott Place in today's street data.
Fire Department Hose Co. No. 1 on Kearny Av.; reservoir not in use in block 4; Nichols Beaver Farm.

Map, 100 ft. Prospect Av to Arlington Av, Sunset Av to Belleville Turnpike: Ilford, Hendel, Melrose Av, Kearny Av (Ridge Road today), Franklin, Abbot, Wesley, Inman, Union, Morgan, Rutherford Pl, Ridge Av (Harding Avenue today); reservoir (not in use). One part.

sheet-93.description: Sheet 93 of the 1922 North Arlington additions, at 100 feet to an inch, shows the south edge of Holy Cross Cemetery and the regular grid laid out below it between Rutherford Place and Schuyler Avenue. The cemetery fills the upper part of the sheet. Below it, Park Avenue and Arlington Avenue (both marked not opened) and Exton Avenue cross Argyle, Beech, Chestnut, Devon, Elm and Forest down to Belleville Turnpike, in blocks 1 to 27 cut into narrow lots of 25 feet. Most of the grid is still vacant: building is limited to a row of dwellings on Rutherford Place, a few houses and sheds in the eastern blocks, and the industrial corner at Belleville Turnpike and Rutherford Place, where Samuel M. Bamdas fur dressing, the American Celutex Corporation (celluloid storage) and Suterten & Card, makers of prepared roofing stand. A hollow tile works sits on the cemetery line near Schuyler Avenue. Water pipes run along the turnpike, Rutherford Place, Elm and Schuyler. Monroe, Madison and Washington Places are lettered at the right edge where they leave Schuyler Avenue for sheet 94, and Ridge Avenue at the left edge.
notes: Ridge Av. is Harding Avenue today.
Monroe Pl., Madison Pl. and Washington Pl. are Halsey Place, Moore Place and Vanderbilt Place today (see sheet 94).
Arlington Av. survives only as a short street between Rutherford Place and Argyle Place.
Samuel M. Bamdas fur dressing; American Celutex Corp.; Suterten & Card prepared roofing.

Map, 100 ft. Holy Cross Cemetery edge and the grid from Rutherford Pl to Schuyler Av, Park Av to Belleville Turnpike: Argyle, Beech, Chestnut, Devon, Elm, Forest; Park and Arlington Av marked not opened. One part.

sheet-94-1.description: Main part of sheet 94 of the 1922 North Arlington additions, at 100 feet to an inch: the east side of Schuyler Avenue from Monroe Place south to Belleville Turnpike, at the south-east corner of the borough. In the north, Monroe Place, Madison Place and Washington Place run east from Schuyler Avenue to Palisade Avenue, forming blocks 1, 3 and 4 and a row of lots along Washington Place, all laid out in narrow lots and almost entirely vacant apart from two dwellings at the Schuyler Avenue corner. The rest of the part is open land: block 5, and block 6 with the Seaboard Metal Corporation solder and babbitt metal works (a corrugated iron foundry, storage building and office), and a storage building near the turnpike. Park, Arlington and Exton Avenues are lettered at the west edge where they meet Schuyler Avenue from sheet 93. The part is separated from the inset (part 2) by a heavy line.
notes: Monroe Pl., Madison Pl., Washington Pl. and Palisade Av. lie where Halsey Place, Moore Place, Vanderbilt Place and Truman Road run today, but only Washington Pl. matches its modern counterpart in position; the drawn Monroe and Madison Places and Palisade Avenue are 13 to 27 m from the modern streets and were not used as control.

Placed from junctions along Schuyler Avenue only (Park, Exton, Washington Pl. and Belleville Turnpike); the blocks east of Schuyler are placed by extrapolation at the atlas scale. Low confidence away from Schuyler Avenue.
Seaboard Metal Corp., solder and babbitt manufacturing.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (left): east side of Schuyler Av from Monroe Pl to Belleville Turnpike with Madison Pl, Washington Pl, Palisade Av and the Seaboard Metal Corp works. Part 2 (upper right, inset behind a heavy line, drawn with north nearly up): Schuyler Av in Kearny between Quincy Pl and Nassau Pl, with Arlington Av and John Hay Av (adjoins Kearny sheets 55 and 75), about 1.8 km south of part 1. Monroe/Madison/Washington Pl and Palisade Av lie near today's Halsey/Moore/Vanderbilt Pl and Truman Road, but only Washington = Vanderbilt matches in position; part 1 is placed from Schuyler Av junctions only. Part 2 (Kearny) placed by a helmert on three Schuyler Av junctions (two hand-picked).

sheet-94-2.description: Inset on sheet 94 of the 1922 North Arlington additions, behind a heavy line in the upper right and drawn with north nearly straight up, at 100 feet to an inch. It does not show North Arlington but a strip of Kearny about 1.8 km to the south: the east side of Schuyler Avenue between Quincy Place and Nassau Place, with Arlington Avenue and John Hay Avenue running south-east from Schuyler into blocks 7, 8 and 9. The lots are narrow and partly built with frame dwellings, a few brick-veneered houses, stores and garages, and a bakery on John Hay Avenue. The south-eastern limit of the blocks is marked as an arbitrary line, and the adjoining sheets 55 and 75 of the main volume are referenced in the margins, with the open block 2 west of Nassau Place.
notes: Located in Kearny, on Schuyler Avenue between Quincy Place and King Street; the reference box was extended south to 40.745 to include it.
Placed by a helmert transformation on three junctions along Schuyler Avenue (one detected, two hand-picked); low confidence.
Nassau Pl. is not in today's street data east of Schuyler Avenue; King Street meets Schuyler from the west at about the same place.
